findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering `AuditLogEntry` by `-datetime`, but this paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the `datetime` field. `build_cursor` invokes this method after fetching the first page, so any authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` and audit-log rows will raise a TypeError rather than return a response. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible datetime cursor serialization/conversion (or the endpoint must use a datetime-aware optimized paginator).

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets cause Django queryset slicing errors
findings.body: The advanced path deliberately passes a negative `start_offset` to a Django QuerySet. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`; it does not implement the boundary behavior claimed in the comment. Since cursor offsets are parsed from client-provided cursor strings, an authorized caller can trigger a 500 response with a negative offset. Reject invalid offsets or normalize them before slicing rather than passing them to the ORM.
